chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted on the authority of Ja'far ibn Malik al-Kufi, who said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mada'eni narrated to me, from Fadl ibn Kathir, from Ali ibn Musa Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever meets a poor Muslim and greets him differently from how he greets the rich, will meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection while He is angry with him.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of greeting the poor differently than the rich?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (a.s.) highlights the spiritual danger of social stratification in religious etiquette, warning that treating the poor with less reverence than the wealthy incurs divine displeasure. This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* underscores the Shia emphasis on egalitarianism and sincerity (*ikhlas*) in worship, where social status does not dictate spiritual worth.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-202 Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted on the authority of Abi Ja’far Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Kufi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mada’eni, on the authority of Fadhl ibn Kathir that Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) said, "
Whoever sees a poor person and greets him in a manner different from that with which he greets a rich man will visit God on the Resurrection Day while God is angry with him."
